{"id": "cdaf57ee-b564-4237-9c29-327973dde734", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_PHlRqSlPhtkkVFgnd0eErx", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Streamline petabyte-scale data migrations with Cloud Write mode on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP | AWS Storage Blog\",\"context\":\"### FSx for ONTAP tiering policies\\\\n\\\\nFSx for ONTAP volumes can be configured to automatically tier data between the SSD storage tier to the capacity pool storage tier as shown in *Figure 2:* This tiering process runs continuously in the background, and the time it takes varies depending on the configured tiering policy and the amount of data that needs to be moved. If the data being migrated into the SSD storage tier is being written faster than the rate at which the background tiering process can move it to the capacity pool tier, then the migration halts because FSx for ONTAP prioritizes front-end traffic over the background tiering task. Adding to this challenge, if this SSD space fills to >98%, then capacity pool tiering is halted until capacity is freed on the SSD storage tier.\\\\n\\\\nThe FSx for ONTAP guide to configuring data tiering policies can help you navigate these options.\\\\n\\\\n*Figure 2: FSx for ONTAP volume data tiering*\\\\n\\\\n**Choose from four tiering policies** to govern tiering:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Snapshot-only:** (Default value) Moves cold snapshots to the capacity pool storage tier. The minimum cooling period is two days, with a valid range of 2 \u2013183 days.\\\\n2. **Auto**: Moves cold user data and snapshots to the capacity pool storage tier based on your access patterns. The default tiering minimum cooling period is 31 days and applies to the entire volume, for both the active file system and the Snapshot copies. Valid cooling period values are 2\u2013183 days.\\\\n3. **All**: (*required for Cloud Write) Moves all user data blocks in both the active file system and Snapshot copies to the capacity pool tier. The tiering minimum cooling period doesn\u2019t apply, because the data moves to the capacity pool tier as soon as the tiering scan runs, and you can\u2019t modify the setting.\\\\n4. **None**: Keeps a volume\u2019s data in the SSD storage tier, preventing it from being moved to the capacity pool tier. The tiering minimum cooling period doesn\u2019t apply, because the data never moves, and you can\u2019t modify the setting\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/streamline-petabyte-scale-data-migrations-with-cloud-write-mode-on-amazon-fsx-for-netapp-ontap/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Volume storage capacity\",\"context\":\"### Volume tiering policies\\\\n\\\\nYou determine how to use your FSx for ONTAP file system\u2019s storage tiers by\\\\nchoosing the tiering policy for each of volume on the file system. You choose the\\\\ntiering policy when you create a volume, and you can modify it at any time with\\\\nthe Amazon FSx console, AWS CLI, API, or using NetApp management tools. You can\\\\nchoose from one of the following policies that determine which data, if any, is\\\\ntiered to the capacity pool storage.\\\\n\\\\n**Note:**\\\\n\\\\nTiering can move your file data and snapshot data to the capacity pool tier. However,\\\\nfile metadata always remains on the SSD tier. For more information, see\\\\nHow SSD storage is used.\\\\n\\\\n* **Auto** \u2013 This policy moves all cold\\\\n data\u2014user data and snapshots\u2014to the capacity pool tier. The cooling rate of\\\\n data is determined by the policy\\'s cooling period, which by default is 31\\\\n days, and is configurable to values between 2\u2013183 days. When the\\\\n underlying cold data blocks are read randomly (as in typical file access),\\\\n they are made hot and written to the primary storage tier. When cold data\\\\n blocks are read sequentially (for example, by an antivirus scan), they\\\\n remain cold and remain on the capacity pool storage tier. This is the\\\\n default policy when creating a volume using the Amazon FSx console.\\\\n* **Snapshot Only** \u2013 This policy moves only\\\\n snapshot data to the capacity pool storage tier. The rate at which snapshots\\\\n are tiered to the capacity pool is determined by the policy\\'s cooling\\\\n period, which by default is set to 2 days, and is configurable to values\\\\n between 2\u2013183 days. When cold snapshot data are read, they are made\\\\n hot and written to the primary storage tier. This is the default policy when\\\\n creating a volume using the AWS CLI, Amazon FSx API, or the NetApp ONTAP\\\\n CLI.\\\\n* **All** \u2013 This policy marks all user data and\\\\n snapshot data as cold, and stores it in the capacity pool tier. When data\\\\n blocks are read, they remain cold and are not written to the primary storage tier.\\\\n When data is written to a volume with the **All** tiering policy,\\\\n it is still initially written to the SSD storage tier, and is tiered\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/volume-storage-capacity.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Migrating file shares to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP using AWS DataSync | AWS Storage Blog\",\"context\":\"## Get to know your volume data tiering policies\\\\n\\\\nAmazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP automatically transitions data between your system\u2019s SSD and capacity pool storage tiers, based on your data access patterns. With data tiering, you can achieve SSD levels of performance for your workload while paying for SSD storage for only a small fraction of your data. As a result, you need to provision primary SSD storage only for the active portion of your dataset, with the rest of your data stored in lower-cost capacity pool storage.\\\\n\\\\nEach volume in your Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system has a data tiering policy associated with it. This tiering policy determines how the data within that volume is transitioned between the primary tier and the capacity pool tier. You can choose from one of four tiering policies outlined in the FSx for NetApp ONTAP managing volumes documentation. In this post, I focus on the **Auto** and **All** policies for migrations.\\\\n\\\\n* **Auto** moves cold user data blocks in both the active file system and the snapshot copies to the storage pool tier. If data is read from the capacity pool tier in a random fashion, the cold data blocks in the capacity tier become hot and move to the primary storage tier. If read by sequential reads, such as those associated with index and antivirus scans, the cold data blocks stay cold and do not move to the primary storage tier.\\\\n* **All** moves cold user data blocks in both the snapshot copies and the active file system to the storage pool tier. If read, cold data blocks on the storage pool tier stay cold and are not written back to the primary storage tier.\\\\n\\\\nYou can set a specific cooling period for the Snapshot Only and Auto policies that range from 2\u2013183 days with a default of 2 days and 31, respectively\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/storage/migrating-file-shares-to-amazon-fsx-for-netapp-ontap-using-aws-datasync/\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be.
